newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish 1-yr, 18-mo bill yields seen falling a bit.
newsitem.headline: Spanish 1-yr, 18-mo bill yields seen falling a bit.

text.p: Spanish one-year and 18-month Treasury bill yields could fall at auction on Wednesday from the previous auction on June 25, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The grey market is working with prices slightly lower than marginal yields of the latest auction (two weeks ago). I think we could see good demand around 4.95/96 percent on both the one-year and the 18-month maturities," a dealer said.
On June 25, the Treasury set a marginal yield at 5.001 percent for one-year bills and at 4.997 percent for 18-months.
On the grey market, these bills were traded earlier this morning at around to 4.94/96 and 4.91/95 percent respectively.
Later this week, the Spanish Treasury is facing bills maturing for around 600 billion pesetas, and dealers added the amount of the new sale should top a similar amount.
"Investment trusts and retailers have a heavy demand. I do not think the Treasury will have any problem to sell a similar amount," another dealer added.
A few dealers added it was likely to see greater demand in the 18-month maturity.
"The 18-month bills are the ones attracting more buying interest from both investment trusts and final clients," he said.
